n: After teaching and organizing the church in Gideon, Alma returns home to Zarahemla to rest — even prophets need rest.

f.w: many things which cannot be written
f.g: Mormon’s record is an abridgment; much was left out.

n: So ends the ninth year of the judges (about 83 BC).
In the tenth year Alma travels west of the river Sidon to the land of Melek, near the wilderness border.

f.g: Later a place of refuge for the people of Ammon.

n: He teaches throughout Melek according to the holy order of God.
People come from all over the region and are baptized — a very successful mission.

f.w: they were baptized throughout all the land
f.g: A sharp contrast to the reception Alma will soon get in Ammonihah.

n: Then Alma travels three days north to the city of Ammonihah.
Mormon explains a Nephite custom: lands and cities were named after whoever first settled them.

f.w: after the name of him who first possessed them

n: Alma begins preaching in Ammonihah.

f.g: Ammonihah was a stronghold of the order of Nehor.

n: Satan had a strong grip on the people’s hearts, so they refused to listen.

f.w: Satan had gotten great hold upon the hearts

n: Alma “wrestles” with God in mighty prayer, pleading for the Spirit to touch these people and for the chance to baptize them.
The people mock him: they know who he is, but they don’t belong to his church and dismiss its teachings as foolish traditions.
They point out that Alma has no authority over them — not in religion, and no longer in government, since he gave up the judgment seat.

f.w: thou art not the chief judge over us

n: They insult him, spit on him, and throw him out of the city. Alma heads toward the city of Aaron.
Weighed down with sorrow over Ammonihah’s wickedness, Alma is met by an angel.

f.g: Alma grieved for the people, not merely for his own mistreatment.

n: The angel tells Alma to rejoice: he has been faithful ever since receiving his first message from God. In fact, this is the same angel who had stopped him years before.

f.w: I am he that delivered it unto you

n: The angel commands Alma to go back and preach again — with a warning that without repentance the Lord will destroy the city.

f.w: except they repent the Lord God will destroy them

n: The angel reveals that Ammonihah’s people are plotting to destroy the liberty of the Nephites — contrary to God’s laws.

f.w: destroy the liberty of thy people

n: Alma obeys immediately, returning by a different route — the south entrance — perhaps to avoid being recognized.

f.g: Compare Jonah, who fled from a similar call; Alma obeys at once.

n: Hungry from fasting, Alma asks a man for food as a humble servant of God.
The man answers that an angel had told him in a vision to receive this prophet, and he welcomes Alma, sure that Alma will bless his household.

f.w: an angel said in a vision

n: The man is Amulek, and he serves Alma bread and meat.
Alma eats, blesses Amulek and his household, and thanks God.

f.w: he blessed Amulek and his house

n: Alma introduces himself as high priest over the church.

f.w: the high priest over the church

n: He explains that he had been rejected here and was ready to leave the land forever.

f.w: set my back towards this land
f.g: Turn away and leave for good.

n: But he was commanded to return and testify against the people’s sins.
Alma blesses Amulek for feeding him, revealing he had been fasting many days.
Alma stays with Amulek many days before beginning to preach — perhaps teaching and preparing his new companion.
Meanwhile the city grows even more wicked.
The Lord calls both Alma and Amulek to warn the people: repent, or face his fierce anger.

f.g: Amulek is now a fellow missionary, providing a second witness.

n: Alma and Amulek go out, filled with the Holy Ghost.
They are given power that no prison could hold them or anyone kill them — but they would not use it until bound and imprisoned, so God’s power could be shown.

f.w: they could not be confined in dungeons

n: They begin preaching and prophesying with the Spirit and power the Lord gave them.

f.w: according to the spirit and power
